name: Agent wallets compared
description: Agent wallets and agent payment accounts already listed in the directory. Not documented means the linked page does not state the fact. Rows are alphabetical by product.
attribution: The Agent Economy agent wallets (https://theagenteconomy.si/data/agent-wallets.json), licensed under CC BY 4.0.
inclusion: A row is a payment rails listing tagged wallets, plus Shop MCP, Stripe link-cli, Stripe Treasury for agents, and Stabletrust API. Those four are included because their provider pages describe a wallet or a payment account an agent spends from. Rows stay alphabetical.

legend.Documented: The linked page states the fact.
legend.Not documented: The linked page does not state the fact. The cell includes the day that page was read.

title: Agent wallets compared

guidance.text: Pick Coinbase Agentic Wallet if you need USDC and x402. The CLI page says the wallet holds USDC, pays x402 services, sets caps per session and per transaction, and keeps private keys in Coinbase infrastructure.

Pick Hedera Agent Accounts if you need an owner funded spending account with a daily cap and a per transaction maximum. The 8 October 2026 post states those limits, payment in HBAR or USDC, and a mainnet target of Q2 2027.
Pick Kite Agent Passport if you need a passkey approved session on a wallet funded in USDC.e. The payments page states a per transaction maximum, a total budget, and x402 pricing for the paid call.
Pick MetaMask Agent Wallet if you need Guard Mode allowlists and a rolling 24 hour outflow limit with 2FA outside that policy. The trading modes page states those controls.

Pick Polygon Agent CLI if you need an embedded wallet that pays x402 under a stated per call cap. The CLI reference says the default per call limit is $1 and the rolling 24 hour total is $10, and session logout revokes that install.

Pick Shop MCP if you need a card issued for one approved purchase. The approvals page says Shop gives the agent card details paid by the saved card, approval_limit is the most that card can be charged, and cancel does not revoke a card already issued.

Pick Skyfire if you need a pay token whose amount is the maximum a seller can charge against a buyer wallet. The tokenAmount page states that maximum and says it cannot exceed the buyer agent wallet balance.

Pick Stabletrust API if you need a hosted transfer API that sends the agent private key. The API page says to fund a dedicated agent wallet with only what the agent needs, because that key travels with every request.

Pick Stripe link-cli if you need a funded Link balance that can skip approval under a per purchase limit. The support page says the user sets that limit, purchases above it still need approval, and a limit of $0 prevents skipping.
guidance.source_title: Set up a balance for agent wallet purchases

guidance.text: Pick Stripe Treasury for agents if you need a Treasury account through MCP where live money movement waits for approval. The docs mark the money movement tools Public preview and say approval is the default.
Pick Tempo Wallet if you need an MPP payment under a max spend cap. The recipes page says the max spend flag caps one command, and access key limits apply separately to the signing key.

Pick Wavelength if you need a self-custodial Lightning wallet an agent can drive over MCP, with no node or channels to run. The 23 October 2026 post says mainnet is open to everyone as an alpha, and L402 pays per request.
guidance.source_title: Lightning Labs: Wavelength on mainnet, 23 October 2026

custody.text: The CLI page says private keys stay in Coinbase infrastructure. Its capabilities table also calls the wallet a self custody wallet controlled by the agent.

settlement.text: The CLI page says agents hold USDC. Its send examples move USDC on Base and on Solana. The networks row lists Base, Base Sepolia, Polygon, Solana, and Solana Devnet.

protocols.text: The overview says the CLI can send, trade, and pay for x402 services. The MCP pays for x402 services and cannot send or trade. The page does not name MPP, AP2, or ACP.

spend_limits.text: The CLI page states configurable caps per session and per transaction.

human_approval.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The MCP page says the user stays in control of spending limits and fund transfers, and that agents do not have access to sensitive actions. It does not state approval of a payment above a threshold.

revocation.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The CLI welcome page does not describe revoking agent spend or a session.

status.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The overview does not call Agentic Wallet generally available, beta, or preview.

license.text: The MCP FAQ says Agentic Wallet MCP is free, wallet creation is free, and gas fees are free because they are sponsored. x402 service calls vary by service, and Coinbase Onramp uses standard fees. That page does not name a software license.

custody.text: The 8 October 2026 post says the accounts are non custodial and private keys never leave the owner wallet. It says the agent does not hold a balance.

settlement.text: The post says agents can pay in HBAR, USDC, or other Hedera tokens.

protocols.text: The post says Agent Accounts are backed by an MCP server, a REST API, and a relayer, and that they are compatible with x402 purchases. It does not name MPP, AP2, or ACP.

spend_limits.text: The post says the owner sets a total spend limit, a daily cap, a per transaction maximum, and an allowlist of recipients and merchants, written to a smart contract.

human_approval.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The post says the agent can transact without approval of every action. It does not state approval above a threshold.

revocation.text: The post says the owner can pause or revoke an agent's spending from the wallet.

status.text: The 8 October 2026 post says Agent Accounts are coming to testnet in Q4 2026 for limited partner validation. Public testnet access follows in Q1 2027, and mainnet availability is targeted for Q2 2027, pending security review and legal sign-off. The post does not use the words generally available, beta, or preview.

license.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The 8 October 2026 post does not name a software license or a price.

custody.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The payments page says a passkey approves a spending session on a Passport wallet. It does not say who holds the wallet keys.

settlement.text: The payments page says the Passport wallet needs USDC.e on Kite chain before the agent can spend, and that a paid call is made in USDC at the service x402 price.

protocols.text: The service provider guide says Passport agents can pay a service that implements x402 or the Machine Payments Protocol. It does not name AP2, ACP, or MCP.

spend_limits.text: The payments page shows a spending session with a per transaction maximum, a total budget, and a time to live. After passkey approval the agent can spend up to the total until the session expires or the budget runs out.

human_approval.text: The payments page says you open an approval URL and approve the session with a passkey. After that, the agent can spend until the session expires or the budget runs out.

revocation.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The payments page says an approved session lasts until it expires or the budget runs out. It does not describe a call that revokes an active session.

status.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The payments page does not call Agent Passport generally available, beta, or preview.

license.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The payments page does not name a software license or a price.

custody.text: The CLI setup page says a server wallet keeps keys server side in a TEE, and a bring your own wallet signs with a BIP-39 mnemonic that stays under local control.

settlement.text: The documentation index lists transfers of native tokens and ERC-20s, and x402 payments that name an asset, an amount, a network, and a payTo address.

protocols.text: The documentation index includes x402 payments. It does not name MPP, AP2, or ACP.

spend_limits.text: The outflow policy page says the limit caps the total value that can leave the server wallet in a rolling 24 hour window. It applies in Guard Mode when using the server wallet. The page does not state a separate per payment cap.

human_approval.text: The trading modes page says Guard Mode asks for 2FA when a transaction is outside allowlists or would exceed the outflow limit. Beast Mode asks for 2FA on malicious and risky transactions.

revocation.text: The documentation index says mm logout signs out and revokes the CLI session.

status.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The documentation index does not call Agent Wallet generally available, beta, or preview. It labels the plugin system Beta.

license.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The documentation index does not name a software license or a price.

custody.text: The CLI reference calls the wallet embedded and says the address is the same on every chain. It does not say where the key is stored.

settlement.text: The CLI reference documents native sends, token sends, and x402 payments. It says fee selection prefers USDC over native POL when both are available. It does not name one settlement asset for every payment.

protocols.text: The CLI reference documents an x402 pay command. It does not name MPP, AP2, ACP, or MCP.

spend_limits.text: The CLI reference says x402 pay refuses a price above the max usd flag. Without that flag, a price over the $1 per call default needs confirmation, and a rolling 24 hour total is capped at $10. Session mode spends inside an allowance. Owner mode says there are no spend limits at the wallet layer.

human_approval.text: The CLI reference says a price over the $1 per call default fails until the command is rerun with the yes flag. Session mode starts from an allowance the owner approves by signing in.

revocation.text: The CLI reference says wallet logout in session mode revokes that install's access.

status.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The CLI reference does not call the wallet generally available, beta, or preview.

license.text: The repository README states the license is MIT.

custody.text: shop.dev says buyers approve the purchase in Shop Pay and the agent gets a one time credential to complete checkout, including outside Shopify.

settlement.text: The approvals page says that after the shopper approves, Shop gives the agent card details for that purchase, paid by the saved card.

protocols.text: shop.dev says the API speaks UCP through MCP. It also says a Link wallet integration can point LINK_API_BASE_URL and LINK_AUTH_BASE_URL at https://mcp.shop.com/api/link. It does not name x402, MPP, AP2, or ACP.

spend_limits.text: The help page says Allow agent to pay for me can use a weekly, monthly, or total budget.
spend_limits.source_title: Using Shop with AI agents and agentic platforms

human_approval.text: The help page says connected agents prepare checkouts so the buyer can review and approve every purchase. Allow agent to pay for me is optional.
human_approval.source_title: Using Shop with AI agents and agentic platforms

revocation.text: The help page says the buyer can disconnect an agent in Connections and can revoke the Allow agent to pay for me permission at any time.
revocation.source_title: Using Shop with AI agents and agentic platforms

custody.text: The payments page says creating a pay or kya-pay token commits the amount against the buyer's wallet, and settlement moves funds from the buyer's wallet to the seller's wallet. The page does not say who holds the keys.

settlement.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The payments page describes settlement between the buyer wallet and the seller wallet, and a $1.00 threshold for faster settlement. It does not name the asset.

protocols.text: The KYAPay tokens page says Skyfire issued tokens conform to the open KYAPay protocol. It does not name x402, MPP, AP2, ACP, or MCP.

spend_limits.text: The tokenAmount page says the value is the maximum the seller can charge, and it must be less than or equal to the balance in the buyer agent wallet. The page does not state a daily, weekly, or session budget.

human_approval.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The tokenAmount page does not state human approval above a spend threshold.

revocation.text: The payments page says deactivating an account stops new tokens. Pay or kya-pay tokens already issued stay chargeable until they expire, plus a 24 hour grace period.

status.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The KYAPay tokens page does not call Skyfire generally available, beta, or preview.

license.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The KYAPay tokens page does not name a software license or a price.

custody.text: The API page says requests send privateKey, and it says to use a dedicated agent wallet funded with only what the agent needs because that private key travels with every request.

settlement.text: The quickstart deposits USDC on Base Sepolia. The page says mainnet transfers and withdrawals on Arbitrum One, Base, and Ethereum charge a protocol fee in ETH. Amounts and balances are encrypted onchain and wallet addresses stay visible.

protocols.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The API page does not name x402, MPP, AP2, ACP, or MCP.

spend_limits.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The API page does not state an owner set cap or a period budget. It says amounts below 0.01 of a token are rejected.

human_approval.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The API page does not state human approval of a transfer.

revocation.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The API page does not describe a revoke call for the wallet or its key.

status.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The API page lists mainnet chains and does not call the API generally available, beta, or preview.

license.text: The API page says the API is open source at github.com/Fairblock/stabletrust-api. It does not name an SPDX license or a price.

custody.text: The Link wallet page says Link returns a payment credential and the customer's real card or bank number is never exposed. Credential types on that page are a virtual card, a shared payment token, and a Link pay token.

settlement.text: Tempo's Link story says Link balance, introduced on 26 October 2026, settles in stablecoins on Tempo. People add money and set a limit per purchase, and the agent spends within that limit without asking each time.
settlement.source_title: Link gives personal agents a budget to spend, powered by stablecoins on Tempo

protocols.text: The Link wallet page names Machine Payments Protocol for a shared payment token, and it names WebMCP for a Stripe enabled checkout. It does not name x402, AP2, or ACP.

spend_limits.text: The README limits table caps one spend request at $500, written as 50,000 cents. It also lists a daily spend of $500 and a 30 day spend of $20,000.

human_approval.text: The Link balance support page says the user sets a per purchase limit. The agent can skip approval at or under that limit. A purchase above it still needs approval. Setting the limit to $0 prevents skipping.
human_approval.source_title: Set up a balance for agent wallet purchases

revocation.text: The README says spend request cancel revokes the payment credential. It does not cancel the subscription with the merchant.

status.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The README does not call Link's wallet generally available, beta, or preview. A section labeled beta describes a separate identity SDK in the same repository.

custody.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The Treasury for agents page does not say who holds account keys. It says an agent connects to a Treasury account through Stripe's MCP server at https://mcp.stripe.com.

settlement.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The page says convert currency converts funds between currencies inside a Treasury account, and send money sends money from that account to a recipient. It does not name one settlement asset.

protocols.text: The page says an agent connects through Stripe's MCP server at https://mcp.stripe.com. It does not name x402, MPP, AP2, or ACP.

spend_limits.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The page does not state a current per payment cap or a period budget.

human_approval.text: The page says that by default you need to review and approve any agent action that results in live money movement.

revocation.text: The page says an authorized MCP client can be revoked from OAuth sessions by selecting Revoke access. Revoking a session removes access only for the account and environment being viewed.

status.text: The page marks the balance summary, convert currency, send money, setup recipient, and transfer money tools as Public preview.

license.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The page does not name a software license or a price.

custody.text: The agent wallet guide says an agent's wallet on Tempo is an access key the agent generates and holds. The account signers authorize that key. The page says not to give the agent the account key.

settlement.text: The guide's spending limit example is 50 of a stablecoin a day, and the code comment calls that amount 50 OUSD. The same page says the interactive demo pays test AlphaUSD on the Tempo Accounts devnet.

protocols.text: The pay with the CLI guide says the CLI handles the MPP challenge and payment retry. It does not name x402, AP2, ACP, or MCP.
protocols.source_title: Tempo guide to paying with the CLI

spend_limits.text: The recipes page says the max spend flag caps one command's payment spending, and access key limits apply separately to the signing key.

human_approval.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The agent wallet guide says the account signers authorize the access key. It does not state a later approval above a spend threshold.

revocation.text: The agent wallet guide says the signers revoke the key by its saved address.

status.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The agent wallet guide does not call Tempo Wallet generally available, beta, or preview. It says that until T14, a configurable account can authorize an agent key only on the devnet.

license.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The wallet recipes page does not name a software license or a price.

custody.text: The system page says the client holds the user's keys and signs payments. The coordination service never has unilateral control of funds, and exit moves the balance back to the Bitcoin blockchain without anyone's permission.

settlement.text: The 23 October 2026 post says humans and agents can pay and get paid in bitcoin over Lightning, with stablecoins coming soon.
settlement.source_title: Lightning Labs: Wavelength on mainnet, 23 October 2026

protocols.text: The 23 October 2026 post says wavecli mcp serve exposes the wallet as MCP tool calls, and L402 charges sats per request with no signup and no API key. It does not name x402, MPP, or AP2.
protocols.source_title: Lightning Labs: Wavelength on mainnet, 23 October 2026

spend_limits.text: The 23 October 2026 post caps each mainnet account at 300,000 sats and each VTXO at 50,000 sats. It does not state a per agent spend limit, budget, or payee allowlist.
spend_limits.source_title: Lightning Labs: Wavelength on mainnet, 23 October 2026

human_approval.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-30. The 23 October 2026 post says an agent pays with no human approving each transaction. It does not state approval above a spend threshold.
human_approval.source_title: Lightning Labs: Wavelength on mainnet, 23 October 2026

revocation.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-30. The bakemacaroon page can set a client side expiry on a macaroon. It does not document revoking a baked macaroon.

status.text: The 23 October 2026 post says Wavelength is now live on mainnet for everyone and that this is still an alpha.
status.source_title: Lightning Labs: Wavelength on mainnet, 23 October 2026
